title: Add-to-calendar links truncate event names containing & or #
body:
### Issue Summary

The "Add to calendar" links on the booking success page do not URI-encode the event name (Google Calendar and Microsoft Office) or the event name and description (Microsoft Outlook, which uses `encodeURI`). Reserved characters such as `&`, `#`, `+` and `=` end the query parameter early.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an event type with the event name `Q&A #1` and a description that contains `a&b=c`.
2. Book the event.
3. On the booking success page, select "Google Calendar", "Microsoft Office" or "Microsoft Outlook".

### Actual Results

- The Google Calendar link contains `text=Q&A #1`, so the title is `Q` and `A` becomes a separate, unknown parameter.
- The Outlook link uses `encodeURI`, which keeps `&`, `#`, `+` and `=`, so the same truncation happens for the subject and the body.

### Expected Results

- The calendar form opens with the full event name and description.

### Technical details

- Code: `packages/features/bookings/lib/getCalendarLinks.ts`, functions `buildGoogleCalendarLink`, `buildMicrosoftOfficeLink` and `buildMicrosoftOutlookLink`.
- The description and location are already encoded with `encodeURIComponent` in the Google Calendar and Microsoft Office links.

### Evidence

A unit test that parses each generated link with `URLSearchParams` fails on current `main` for the event name `Q&A #1 + 100% é` and passes with `encodeURIComponent` applied.
